fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. God says, “…I will hold you responsible for his blood.” The “you” is Ezekiel, the one who was supposed to warn the man and didn't. That's what makes the watchman's job so serious. It's a heavy line.

Not what the text says, friend. When Ezekiel warns him, God says “…you will have saved yourself.” The responsibility for the man's blood is in the case where Ezekiel stays quiet (Ezekiel 3:18). Here the watchman did his part.

That's a reasonable guess, baker, but this verse doesn't say it. It says the man “…will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved yourself.” Ezekiel's warning was given, and God says he has saved himself. The verse stops there.

Yes, baker. Ezekiel says, “…the glory of the LORD was present there, like the glory I had seen by the River Kebar, and I fell facedown.” He had seen glory like that before. Even so, it puts him on the ground.

Good guess, friend, but the temple isn't in this passage. God says, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.” Think about that. You hire a watchman, and his first order is to stay home. I'd have asked if there was a window.
Nice try, friend, but a stuck tongue won't touch his eyes. It keeps him from speaking. God says Ezekiel will be “…silent and unable to rebuke them…” The glory doesn't come up in this verse at all.
